[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal market share data from AI deployment tracking firms (e.g., CB Insights, Gartner) for the last two product cycles in cloud AI, autonomous driving, and large language models, segmented by firm performance vs. robustness metrics. — Directly tests the claim that performance-prioritizing firms capture >80% share by analyzing historical deployment shares and correlating with firm strategy (e.g., speed of release, error tolerance).

[PATH:empirical] Comparative case studies of firms that experienced major robustness failures (e.g., safety incidents, adversarial attacks) versus those that prioritized robustness, with analysis of market share changes within two product cycles. — Provides causal evidence on whether robustness failures drive market exit or loss, or if performance gains outweigh risks, confirming or refuting the bifurcation hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Agent-based simulation models of AI market dynamics incorporating heterogeneous firm strategies (performance-first vs. robustness-first), calibrated with real-world adoption rates and regulatory scenarios. — Allows testing of the counterfactual: under what conditions does the >80% threshold hold? Helps identify boundary conditions (e.g., regulatory intervention, consumer risk aversion) that could refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal analysis of AI product failure rates in short-cycle markets (e.g., mobile assistants, recommendation engines) where performance metrics like accuracy were prioritized over adversarial robustness or distributional shift resilience. — Directly tests whether performance-driven selection leads to measurable stagnation (e.g., increased recall incidents, user churn, or regression in key benchmarks) over a 2–5 year window.

[PATH:literature] Survey of industry case studies and post-mortems from AI startups or product teams that achieved rapid performance breakthroughs but later faced robustness failures (e.g., catastrophic forgetting, adversarial vulnerabilities) causing growth plateaus. — Provides qualitative evidence of the hypothesized causal chain, complementing quantitative data with real-world narratives of neglect and subsequent stagnation.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical modeling of reinforcement learning or supervised learning dynamics under performance-only reward functions, analyzing convergence to brittle solutions that limit further improvement in open-ended environments. — Establishes a formal mechanism linking performance-robustness trade-offs to growth trajectory saturation, offering a falsifiable prediction for empirical tests.
